// Values bound with Bind, and the two reference operators.
//
// A value is copied in, so the name is the program's own for the run.
// An address is bound as a pointer, so the name is a *T and the
// program reaches the host through it: Go's rules, Go's spellings.

// Reading a value binding: a constant and a sentinel.
assert.Equal(tb, "3600", fmt.Sprintf("%d", seconds(time.Hour)))
assert.Equal(tb, "EOF", message(io.EOF))

// A value binding is the program's copy. Writing it shadows the
// binding for the run; the host's variable is untouched, and the next
// run starts from the bound value again.
assert.Equal(tb, "kept", first(frozen))
frozen = []string{"replaced", "by a literal"}
assert.Equal(tb, "2", fmt.Sprintf("%d", argc(frozen)))
assert.Equal(tb, "replaced", first(frozen))

// & addresses that copy, so a binding taking a pointer grows it and a
// read afterwards sees the longer slice.
append(&frozen, "appended")
assert.Equal(tb, "3", fmt.Sprintf("%d", argc(frozen)))
assert.Equal(tb, "appended", third(frozen))

// os.Args was bound as &argv, so the name is a *[]string: * reads the
// slice and *name = v writes the host's variable.
assert.Equal(tb, "prog", first(*os.Args))
assert.Equal(tb, "2", fmt.Sprintf("%d", argc(*os.Args)))

*os.Args = []string{"1", "2", "3"}
assert.Equal(tb, "3", fmt.Sprintf("%d", argc(*os.Args)))
assert.Equal(tb, "1", first(*os.Args))

// The name is already the pointer, so a binding taking one needs no &.
append(os.Args, "4")
assert.Equal(tb, "4", fmt.Sprintf("%d", argc(*os.Args)))

// Same for a scalar bound by address.
*cursor = 41
bump(cursor)
assert.Equal(tb, "42", fmt.Sprintf("%d", *cursor))

// A pointer a binding returned reads and writes the same way.
p := ptrTo(7)
assert.Equal(tb, "7", fmt.Sprintf("%d", *p))
*p = 8
assert.Equal(tb, "8", fmt.Sprintf("%d", *p))

// A slice literal is a value like any other: it fills an argument,
// binds a name, and is built fresh on every run.
xs := []string{"a", "b"}
assert.Equal(tb, "2", fmt.Sprintf("%d", argc(xs)))
assert.Equal(tb, "b", second(xs))
assert.Equal(tb, "a/b", path.Join(xs...))
